chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام when he was asked about salat (prayer) in a ship, and he said: If you are able to go out to the firm ground, then go out. But if you are not able, then perform salat standing; and if you are not able, then perform salat sitting, and seek out the qiblah.

key_terms.السَّفِينَةِ: the ship, the location in which the prayer is being performed
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship being discussed
key_terms.الْجَدَدِ: firm or solid ground to which one may disembark
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of prayer that one must try to face
key_terms.قُعُودًا: sitting, the posture used when standing is not possible
key_terms.قِيَامًا: standing, the preferred posture when able

ai.seo_question: How should salat be performed in a ship according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on performing salat (prayer) in a ship. It establishes a sequence based on ability: pray on firm ground if possible, otherwise standing in the ship, and if unable then sitting, while taking care to determine the qiblah.
